\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شمعة} (shamʿa)}{شمعة (shamʿa)}]{\ar{شمعة} (shamʿa) — a candle}

\label{lesson:AR-C126-shama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a basket, then the Arabic for a box.

Say \textquotedblleft{}he came.\textquotedblright{} (\emph{Jāʾa} — the weak \textbf{\ar{ي}} of its root has dissolved.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شمعة}}
\textbf{\ar{شمعة}} — \emph{shamʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}a candle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شمعة}} (\emph{shamʿa}) is built on \emph{shamʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}wax\textquotedblright{}, a native noun, filed under the root \emph{sh-m-ʿ} (Lane); \emph{shamʿa} is one candle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}
